angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 797,968 km at 106.48 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.3912 +/- 0.0214 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 106.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.147 +/- 0.028 solar radii from Damasso et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 224018 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.118D/abstract): 797,968 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.013 +/- 0.069 solar masses from Damasso et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 224018 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.118D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5784 +/- 60 K from Damasso et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 224018 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.118D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Damasso et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 224018 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.118D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-224018.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.325, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
